This agreement is between {{parties.company_name}} of {{parties.company_address}} ("the Company") and {{parties.supplier_name}} of {{parties.supplier_address}} ("the Supplier").

In this agreement:
- "Supplier Personnel" means every individual the Supplier provides to carry out work under this agreement, whether the Supplier employs them, engages them on another basis or obtains them through a third party approved under this agreement.
- "Site" means a location listed in this agreement or in an order or change the parties agree in writing.
- "End Client" means the Company's customer at a Site.

The Supplier enters into this agreement as an independent business. Nothing in it makes the Supplier, or any of the Supplier Personnel, an employee of the Company, and nothing in it makes the parties partners or agents of each other.

title: Legal duties that stay with each party
subject: b2b

all.body:
This agreement allocates practical responsibilities between the parties. Allocating a task to one party does not remove or transfer a duty that the law places on the other. Each party remains responsible for its own legal obligations, whatever this agreement says.

In particular:
- **Health and safety.** Each party keeps its own duties under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999 towards anyone affected by its activities, including Supplier Personnel working at a Site the Company controls or arranges. The parties will share the risk information each needs and co-operate and co-ordinate their arrangements.
- **Working time.** The party that employs or pays an individual keeps its duties under the Working Time Regulations 1998. The party that sets or changes shift patterns will not knowingly schedule anyone in a way that breaches the limits or rest entitlements in those Regulations, and each party will give the other the hours records it needs to check this.
- **Security licensing.** Under the Private Security Industry Act 2001 it is an offence to carry out licensable conduct without a valid SIA licence and to use or supply unlicensed operatives. Each party remains responsible for making sure that no one it deploys, or allows to work, carries out licensable activity without the right licence.
- **Right to work.** Each party remains responsible for any right-to-work check the law requires it to make.

Nothing in this agreement limits or excludes either party's liability for death or personal injury caused by its negligence, for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, or for anything else the law does not allow to be limited or excluded (see section 2 of the Unfair Contract Terms Act 1977).

The Supplier will indemnify the Company against losses, fines, penalties, claims and reasonable costs the Company suffers because of:
- any claim by Supplier Personnel, or by HMRC or another authority, about the pay, tax, National Insurance contributions, holiday pay, pension contributions or other employment rights of Supplier Personnel, except to the extent the Company caused it;
- the Supplier providing anyone who does not hold a valid SIA licence of the right type for the work, or who does not have the right to work in the UK;
- the Supplier's breach of the data protection or confidentiality terms of this agreement.

Subject to the first paragraph and the indemnity above, each party's total liability to the other arising out of or in connection with this agreement in any contract year is limited to {{liability.cap}}. Neither party is liable to the other for loss of profit or indirect or consequential loss.

A party claiming under this clause must tell the other promptly about the claim, take reasonable steps to limit its loss, and not settle a third-party claim without consulting the other.

The Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006 ("TUPE") can transfer employees automatically to a new employer when a service starts, moves between contractors or ends. Whether TUPE applies depends on the facts at the time. This agreement does not assume that it will or will not apply.

Before this agreement starts, when the services or the Supplier Personnel change significantly, and when it is due to end, the parties will assess together whether TUPE may apply. Each party will give the other, promptly and accurately, the information it reasonably needs for that assessment, and the employee liability information TUPE requires a transferring employer to give.

The Supplier will not, without the Company's written agreement, make changes intended to alter which of its employees are assigned to the work covered by this agreement during the period before it ends. Any agreement about who bears the cost of a transfer must be made in writing and checked by a legal adviser.

Either party may end this agreement by giving the other at least {{termination.notice}} written notice.

Either party may end this agreement immediately by written notice if the other:
- commits a serious breach of it which cannot be put right, or which is not put right within {{termination.remedy_period}} of written notice asking for it to be put right;
- becomes insolvent, enters administration, liquidation or any arrangement with its creditors, or stops trading.

The Company may also end this agreement immediately by written notice if the Supplier, or anyone it provides, acts in a way that puts the Company in breach of the law or of the SIA's requirements, or if the Supplier loses any licence, approval or registration this agreement requires it to hold.

Ending this agreement does not affect rights and obligations that have already arisen, or any term intended to continue after it ends, including confidentiality, data protection, liability, insurance for claims already notified, payment of amounts due and return of property.

title: Nature of the supply and management
subject: labour

all.body:
The Supplier supplies Supplier Personnel to the Company to supplement the Company's own workforce. This is a supply of labour, not a subcontract: the Company remains responsible to the End Client for the security services at each Site, and the Supplier does not take responsibility for delivering those services.

While on assignment, Supplier Personnel work under the direction and supervision of the Company. Day-to-day management at each Site is the responsibility of {{management.company_contact}}, or another person the Company names in writing. The Supplier's contact for this agreement is {{management.supplier_contact}}.

The Company will tell each End Client that it uses supplied labour at their Site where the End Client's contract or the SIA's guidance calls for it.

all.body:
The Company will request Supplier Personnel by {{ordering.method}}. Each request will state the Site, dates, shift times, number of people, role, SIA licence category required, any additional training, experience or qualifications needed, and any known health and safety risks of the work and the steps taken to control them.

The Supplier will confirm or decline each request within {{ordering.response_time}}. A request becomes a binding order only when the Supplier confirms it. The Company is not obliged to place any minimum number of orders, and the Supplier is not obliged to accept any request.

Either party may ask to change a confirmed order. A change takes effect when both parties confirm it in writing. The Company may cancel a confirmed shift by giving at least {{ordering.cancellation_notice}} notice. If the Company cancels with less notice, it will pay the Supplier {{ordering.cancellation_charge}}.

Charges for cancelled shifts are between the Company and the Supplier. They do not decide what the Supplier pays any individual for a cancelled shift, which is the Supplier's responsibility under its own contracts and the law.

The Company will pay the Supplier the charge rates set out here: {{rates.schedule}}. The following premiums apply: {{rates.premiums}}. VAT is added where it applies.

The charge rates are the price the Company pays the Supplier for the supply. They are not the pay of Supplier Personnel. The Supplier alone sets and pays the pay of Supplier Personnel, and it is never worked out from the charge rate. The Supplier must pay each person at least the National Minimum Wage or National Living Wage that applies to them, and any pay the agency workers clause requires, whatever the charge rate.

A change to the charge rates must be agreed in writing. A change in the charge rate does not of itself change anyone's pay, and a change in anyone's pay does not of itself change the charge rate.

Supplier Personnel's hours will be recorded on timesheets approved by {{timesheets.approver}}. The Company will approve or query each timesheet promptly. Charges are calculated only on approved hours. A query about hours is handled as a disputed amount under the invoicing clause, and the Supplier remains responsible for paying Supplier Personnel on time while it is resolved.

The Supplier will tell {{attendance.report_to}} as soon as it knows that a confirmed person will not attend or will be late, and at least {{attendance.absence_notice}} before the shift starts where possible.

The Supplier will use reasonable efforts to provide a suitable replacement within {{attendance.replacement_time}}. A replacement must meet the same requirements as the person replaced. If the Supplier cannot fill a confirmed shift, it will tell the Company straight away so that the Company can arrange cover. The Company does not pay for hours not worked.

The Company may ask the Supplier not to supply a particular person again, or to remove them from a Site, if it reasonably considers them unsuitable. It will give the Supplier its reasons in writing. The Company will not make such a request for a reason that would be unlawful discrimination. The Supplier remains responsible for that person's employment and pay.

The Supplier will not pay or engage Supplier Personnel through any umbrella company, personal service company, offshore arrangement or other intermediary unless the further supply chains clause allows it and the Company has approved that intermediary in writing.

The Supplier will give the Company, when asked, reasonable evidence that it is meeting these obligations, which may include confirmation of its PAYE registration, evidence of payment of Supplier Personnel at or above the legal minimum, its holiday pay and pension arrangements, and confirmation that it has no unresolved HMRC enforcement action relevant to this agreement.

The Company, or an auditor it appoints, may inspect the Supplier's records relevant to this agreement on giving at least {{assurance.audit_notice}} notice. The Supplier will co-operate, and will tell the Company promptly if it becomes aware of any failure to meet these obligations.

title: Agency workers: information and equal treatment
subject: labour

all.body:
Where the Agency Workers Regulations 2010 apply, the Supplier is the temporary work agency and the Company is the hirer.

**The Supplier** is responsible for giving Supplier Personnel the basic working and employment conditions they are entitled to, including equal treatment on pay, working time, rest and annual leave once they have completed the statutory qualifying period (12 weeks in the same role with the Company), and for tracking that qualifying period.

**The Company** is responsible for:
- giving Supplier Personnel the same access to collective facilities and amenities, and the same information about vacancies, as comparable workers it employs directly, from their first day;
- giving the Supplier, promptly and in writing, accurate information about the basic working and employment conditions of comparable workers and any changes to them, and the information needed to track the qualifying period;
- co-operating with any request for information from Supplier Personnel under the Regulations.

If equal treatment changes what the Supplier must pay Supplier Personnel, the Supplier may ask to review the charge rates under the charge rates clause. A review of the charge rates never reduces anyone's entitlement under the Regulations.

The parties will agree which of them makes any report required by law (for example to the enforcing authority under the reporting of injuries regulations), and will co-operate with each other's investigations. Either party may escalate a safety concern to the other's named contact at any time.

title: Further supply chains: only with approval
subject: labour

The Supplier will not obtain Supplier Personnel from, or pay them through, another agency, labour provider, umbrella company or other intermediary unless the Company has approved that business in writing in advance.

Before asking for approval, the Supplier will tell the Company the name and registered details of the business, its role in the chain, and how Supplier Personnel will be engaged and paid. The Supplier will provide the Services at these Sites: {{services.sites}}.

The operating hours are: {{services.hours}}.

The required coverage is: {{services.coverage}}. The Supplier will make sure the required coverage is met during the operating hours, with every position filled by a suitably licensed and trained person.

sources.title: SIA: Know the difference between sub-contracting and use of labour

all.body:
The Supplier will be ready to deliver the Services in full from {{services.mobilisation_date}}. Before that date it will complete site surveys, inductions and familiarisation, confirm that every person to be deployed meets the requirements of this agreement, and give the Company the evidence the Company reasonably asks for.

The Supplier will tell the Company straight away if anything is likely to delay mobilisation, and what it is doing about it.

sources.title: SIA: Know the difference between sub-contracting and use of labour

all.body:
The Supplier is responsible for managing and supervising the Services and Supplier Personnel. Its supervision arrangements are: {{management.supervision}}.

The Supplier's contract manager is {{management.supplier_contact}}. The Company's contact is {{management.company_contact}}. Each party will tell the other promptly if its contact changes.

The contacts will review the Services together {{management.review_frequency}}, covering performance, incidents, staffing, health and safety, complaints and any changes needed.

sources.title: SIA: Know the difference between sub-contracting and use of labour

all.body:
The Company will give the Supplier the End Client's requirements for each Site. The Supplier will prepare assignment instructions for each Site that meet those requirements, and will not use them until the Company has approved them in writing. The approved assignment instructions form part of this agreement.

The Supplier will make sure every person it deploys has read and understood the current assignment instructions before working at the Site.

Either party may propose a change to the Services, the assignment instructions, the coverage or the Sites. A proposed change, and any change to the charges it causes, takes effect only when both parties approve it in writing. In an emergency the Supplier will follow reasonable instructions from the Company or the End Client needed to protect people or property, and the parties will record the change in writing as soon as possible.

sources.title: SIA: Know the difference between sub-contracting and use of labour

all.body:
The Company is an SIA approved contractor. Under the SIA's Approved Contractor Scheme, an approved contractor may subcontract designated security services only to another approved contractor, unless the SIA has agreed otherwise.

The Supplier confirms that it holds SIA approved contractor status covering the Services. It will keep that status for as long as this agreement lasts, meet the scheme's requirements in delivering the Services, and tell the Company straight away if its approval is suspended, withdrawn, made subject to conditions or not renewed.

title: SIA Approved Contractor Scheme: SIA permission
subject: subcontract

all.body:
The Company is an SIA approved contractor. Under the SIA's Approved Contractor Scheme, an approved contractor may subcontract designated security services only to another approved contractor, unless the SIA has agreed otherwise. The Supplier is not an approved contractor, and the Company relies on the SIA's permission to subcontract the Services to it.

The Supplier will meet any conditions of that permission, give the Company the information it needs to show the SIA that the Services are managed to the scheme's standard, and tell the Company straight away about anything that could affect the permission.

sources.title: SIA: ACS self-assessment workbook (2026 update)
SIA: Know the difference between sub-contracting and use of labour

all.body:
The Supplier will deliver the Services to these performance measures: {{performance.measures}}.

The Supplier will report to the Company on performance against those measures {{performance.reporting_frequency}}, and straight away about any serious incident, complaint, missed shift or security breach.

If the Supplier fails to meet a performance measure, it will give the Company a written plan to put it right within {{performance.correction_period}}, and carry it out. Repeated or serious failure to meet the performance measures is a serious breach of this agreement.

sources.title: SIA: ACS self-assessment workbook (2026 update)

title: Business continuity, absence and service failure
subject: subcontract

all.body:
The Supplier will maintain a business continuity plan for the Services, covering staff absence, loss of systems and other disruption, and will give it to the Company on request.

The Supplier is responsible for covering absence from its own resources. It will tell the Company within {{continuity.notice}} of becoming aware that any part of the required coverage may not be met, and what it is doing about it.

If the Supplier does not provide any part of the Services, the Company does not pay for that part. If the failure continues after the Company has given the Supplier a reasonable opportunity to put it right, the Company may arrange cover from elsewhere and recover the reasonable extra cost from the Supplier.

sources.title: SIA: ACS self-assessment workbook (2026 update)

all.body:
The Company will pay the Supplier for the Services the charges set out here: {{charges.schedule}}. VAT is added where it applies.

The charges are the price of the Services. The Supplier alone sets and pays the pay of Supplier Personnel, which must be at least the National Minimum Wage or National Living Wage that applies to each person, whatever the charges.

The charges may only change by written agreement, including through an approved change to the Services.

all.body:
The Supplier will keep a register of all keys, access cards, fobs and alarm codes issued to it for the Services, record who holds each one, and give the register to the Company on request.

The Supplier will keep keys and codes secure, never mark keys with the Site address, and only give access to Supplier Personnel who need it for their duties. It will tell the Company straight away if a key, card or code is lost, stolen or may have been compromised, and will pay the reasonable cost of replacement or changing locks or codes where the loss was its fault.

all.body: The Supplier will not subcontract or delegate any part of the Services, or use labour supplied by another business to deliver them, without the Company's prior written approval. The Company may refuse approval at its discretion.

sources.title: SIA: ACS self-assessment workbook (2026 update)
SIA: Know the difference between sub-contracting and use of labour

all.body:
The Supplier may only subcontract part of the Services, or use labour supplied by another business, with the Company's prior written approval of that business. Before asking for approval, the Supplier will tell the Company who the business is, what it will do, and whether it is subcontracting or supplying labour.

Any approved business must meet the same licensing, screening, right-to-work, pay and tax requirements as the Supplier and, where it takes on part of the Services as a subcontractor and the Approved Contractor Scheme requires it, hold approved contractor status. Where the Supplier is an approved contractor, it will not pass any part of the Services to a business that is not, unless the SIA and the End Client have agreed. The Supplier remains fully responsible for everything an approved business does or fails to do.

all.body:
When this agreement or any Site is due to end, the Supplier will co-operate fully in an orderly handover to the Company or a replacement provider for a period of {{exit.assistance_period}} before the end date.

During the handover the Supplier will give the Company up-to-date assignment instructions, key and access registers, incident logs, site records and any other information needed to continue the Services safely, subject to the data protection terms of this agreement.

By the end date the Supplier will return all keys, access cards, codes, equipment, documents and other property of the Company or the End Client, and confirm in writing that it has done so and has not kept any copies except where the law requires it.
